Subject: Unexpected tail latency & 502 spike on our private cluster

Hi Stephanie —

We’re seeing a sudden increase in tail latency (p95 -> ~1.6s, p99 -> ~5.2s) and intermittent 502s from our SilverStrand private deployment starting ~08:45 PDT. This started right after a config rollout that increased the concurrency cap on the cluster (ops change made by our infra team). The errors are impacting our clinician-facing flows.

Short timeline:
- 08:44: config rollout complete
- 08:50: first 502 observed (spike)
- 09:05: sustained p99 high and user complaints

Can your team triage? We need mitigation steps we can apply immediately (fallbacks, routing, or temporary capacity). I’ve looped procurement in case we need a short burst capacity authorization.

Attachments: small traces and timestamps attached (we’ll share full logs if you need them).

Thanks,
Alex Monroe

Subject: Re: Unexpected tail latency & 502 spike on our private cluster

Stef / Alex — quick initial findings from a remote inspection of the metrics SilverStrand sent:

1) KV cache growth: we see sustained growth in KV cache miss latency after the concurrency cap increase. Cold KV fetches are amplifying token latency at tail.
2) Batching mismatch: the recent ops change increased parallel requests per GPU without adjusting batch aggregation thresholds; this causes more small batches and higher per-token overhead.
3) Kernel selection noise: model variant on the node reported occasional kernel fallback to a slower execution path (likely due to memory pressure + sequence length spikes).

Immediate recommended mitigation (safe, low-risk):
- Revert concurrency cap to prior value (ops) OR throttle incoming QPS at the edge by 10–15% (ops/app).
- Force model pin to the quantized variant we already validated (reduces kernel noise).
- Enable temporary aggressive prefix cache warmup for known hot endpoints.
- Reduce batch_size target from 64 to 32 for 30 minutes.

I uploaded a preliminary KV profile (prelim_kv_profile.csv) to the thread and opened SUP-7789 with the triage notes. If the customer agrees, we can also authorize a 1-hour Dedicated burst while we apply the above mitigations and monitor.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal SRE — Redwood Inference

Subject: Incident update & next steps — SilverStrand private cluster

Status update after the burst and mitigations:

What we did (10:30–11:40 PDT):
- Triggered 1-hour Dedicated burst and routed 22% of production QPS to hosted fallbacks.
- Forced pin to quantized model variant on SilverStrand nodes.
- Reduced batch_size target to 32 and enabled more aggressive prefix warmup for hot endpoints.
- Monitored KV cache growth and memory utilization.

Observed impact:
- p99 dropped from 5.2s -> 1.1s within 15 minutes of pin + warmup.
- 502s fell to baseline (mostly due to reduced memory pressure and smaller batches).
- Error rate returned to normal by 11:15 PDT.

Open items / next steps:
- Engineering (Jonas): kernel-level investigation and a patch to prevent fallback to the slower execution path under memory pressure.
- Ops (SilverStrand): revert the concurrency cap change or make it more conservative with a staged rollout.
- Product: schedule a sustained pre-warm job for known hot endpoints to prevent cold-KV amplification.

I’ve attached a draft postmortem (postmortem-draft.md) and added SUP-7789 notes. Recommend a 16:00 PT exec sync to decide on credits & long-term remediation; Stephanie — can you lead the exec ask?

— Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
